edges.mechanism: Rhodiola (SHR-5) inhibits CYP2C9 in humans (21% fall in losartan metabolic ratio) and noncompetitively in vitro; warfarin is a narrow-therapeutic-index CYP2C9 substrate.
edges.evidence: Human probe-drug crossover (n=13) and in vitro data; rat study showed no change in warfarin PK/anticoagulation; no human warfarin study; low certainty

edges.mechanism: CYP2C9 inhibition in humans; authors flag narrow-therapeutic-index substrates such as phenytoin.
edges.evidence: Single human probe study (n=13) plus in vitro mechanism; HMPC judged clinical relevance unclear

edges.mechanism: CYP2C9 and P-gp inhibition; in rabbits losartan AUC almost doubled (Spanakis 2013); in humans the EXP-3174/losartan ratio fell 21%.
edges.evidence: Rabbit PK study plus human probe-drug study; clinical BP consequence not studied

edges.mechanism: Potent in vitro CYP3A4 inhibition (IC50 1.7-3.1 ug/mL), but no change in midazolam metabolism in humans; salidroside alone showed no CYP inhibition.
edges.evidence: In vitro positive, human probe study negative; low certainty of a clinical effect

edges.mechanism: In vitro P-gp inhibition (digoxin transport IC50 16.7-51.7 ug/mL); losartan exposure rose in rabbits.
edges.evidence: In vitro and animal data only; no human P-gp study

edges.mechanism: No PK change with SHR-5 in rats; CYP1A2 (caffeine probe) unaffected in humans.
edges.evidence: Animal and human probe data suggest a negligible interaction

edges.mechanism: Possible pharmacodynamic serotonergic/activating overlap (in vitro MAO inhibition) and CYP/P-gp effects; paroxetine case interpreted as serotonergic syndrome; EudraVigilance reports with sertraline, paroxetine (serotonin syndrome), duloxetine and amitriptyline.
edges.evidence: Case report, pharmacovigilance series and adaptogen-antidepressant chart review (Siwek 2023 abstract does not list Rhodiola-specific cases); low certainty

edges.mechanism: Root extracts inhibit MAO-A (up to 92.5%) and MAO-B in vitro; additive MAO inhibition is theoretical. Isolated salidroside does not inhibit MAO.
edges.evidence: In vitro only; mechanistic inference, no clinical reports found

edges.mechanism: Pharmacovigilance cases with haloperidol (myoclonus, hypoglycaemia, sedation), risperidone and quetiapine combinations; mechanism unclear.
edges.evidence: Case series from pharmacovigilance; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Cases of excessive sedation with diazepam and hypotension with alprazolam when combined with Rhodiola.
edges.evidence: Pharmacovigilance case series cited in HMPC assessment; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Rhodiola/salidroside lower glucose via AMPK in preclinical models; additive glucose lowering possible.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic inference from preclinical review; no human interaction data

edges.mechanism: Aqueous extract lowered SBP in hypertensive rats via beta-endorphin; R. crenulata had no BP effect in human altitude RCTs.
edges.evidence: Animal data plus null human BP data; speculative

edges.mechanism: Rhodiola has CNS-stimulating activity, and nervousness and insomnia are labelled adverse effects; additive activation with amphetamine is plausible.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic inference from review and EU AE listing; no interaction study

edges.mechanism: Combined use in sport RCTs improved explosive power and duel performance; Rhodiola does not alter CYP1A2 caffeine metabolism.
edges.evidence: Several small RCTs; a 2026 trial found no significant CAF x RHO interaction, so synergy not established; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Rhodiola was named a possible co-causative agent in one DILIN ashwagandha liver-injury case; ashwagandha itself causes cholestatic HILI.
edges.evidence: Single case within a case series; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Both are stimulating adaptogens; both are among herbs most often implicated in adverse interactions with psychotropic drugs. Additive stimulation is inferred.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic inference; no combination study

edges.mechanism: Antidepressant/activating profile; case report of mania associated with Rhodiola rosea.
edges.evidence: Case report and mechanistic reviews; WFSBP/CANMAT does not support Rhodiola for mood disorders

edges.mechanism: Safety not established; reproductive toxicity and genotoxicity tests unavailable.
edges.evidence: EU HMPC monograph: use not recommended

edges.mechanism: Safety during lactation not established.
edges.evidence: EU HMPC monograph: use not recommended

edges.mechanism: No safety data from clinical trials in this age group.
edges.evidence: EU HMPC monograph: use not recommended

edges.mechanism: CYP2C9 inhibition by Rhodiola was more pronounced in CYP2C9 extensive metabolizers than in intermediate/poor metabolizers.
edges.evidence: Subgroup of a single 13-person human study; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Not an assay artifact; INR may shift via CYP2C9 inhibition in patients on warfarin.
edges.evidence: Inferred from human CYP2C9 data; no direct INR study
